name: Isolated Oxidative Phosphorylation Complex Disorder
aliases: Isolated Mitochondrial Respiratory Chain Complex Deficiency

criteria.description: Demonstration of isolated deficiency in one oxidative phosphorylation complex enzyme activity in muscle or fibroblasts
Presence of clinical features consistent with mitochondrial disease such as muscle weakness, neurodevelopmental delay, or lactic acidosis
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear or mitochondrial genes encoding subunits or assembly factors of the affected complex
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-negative fibers
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of isolated biochemical deficiency in one OXPHOS complex plus compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; muscle biopsy and biochemical assays remain gold standard.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Isolated deficiency of a single mitochondrial respiratory chain complex enzyme activity
pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by enzymatic assay in muscle or fibroblasts
searchTerms: lack of activity in one mitochondrial enzyme
reduced function of one respiratory chain enzyme
muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
abnormal muscle fibers with red staining

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated blood or cerebrospinal fluid lactate concentration
searchTerms: high lactate levels in blood or spinal fluid
elevated lactic acid in body fluids
increased lactate in blood or CSF

common.notes: Often symmetric and affecting limb girdle muscles
searchTerms: gradual weakness in upper legs and arms

common.notes: May be triggered by metabolic stress
Reported in some isolated complex deficiencies

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to neuronal energy failure
Cerebellar involvement due to mitochondrial dysfunction

rare.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to mitochondrial dysfunction
searchTerms: blood sugar issues from mitochondrial dysfunction
diabetes linked to energy production defects

rare.notes: Rare but possible in some mitochondrial disorders

laboratory: Isolated deficiency of a single respiratory chain complex enzyme activity in muscle or fibroblast assays
Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
imaging: Brain MRI may show basal ganglia or brainstem signal abnormalities
Muscle MRI may reveal selective muscle involvement
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear or mitochondrial genes encoding subunits or assembly factors of the affected complex
Heteroplasmy levels in mitochondrial DNA mutations may correlate with severity
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers
Histochemical staining demonstrating isolated complex deficiency

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple respiratory chain complexes deficient rather than isolated single complex
Marked reduction in mitochondrial DNA copy number
Often presents in infancy with liver failure or myopathy
May involve multiple complexes or generalized mitochondrial dysfunction
Broader clinical phenotype including exercise intolerance and multisystem involvement

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with lactic acidosis
Early onset neurodevelopmental regression with biochemical evidence of isolated complex deficiency
Refractory seizures or stroke-like episodes in context of mitochondrial dysfunction
